weight_direction.s3: Weight is trending in a healthier direction as a natural consequence of reduced emotional eating, improved portion awareness, and eliminated late-night eating. No scale targets set.
weight_direction.graduation: Weight has moved in a healthier direction as a natural byproduct of the behavioral changes. The client does not define success by the scale. Success is measured by the 6 SMART baselines, not pounds.

self_worth.baseline: Self-worth is tied to weight, eating behavior, and appearance. Guilt after eating is frequent. Confidence in ability to change: 4 out of 10.
self_worth.s3: Self-worth is decoupling from the scale. Guilt after eating is less frequent. Confidence: 6-7 out of 10. The client sees evidence that the pattern is changing.
self_worth.graduation: Self-worth is independent of weight. The client's identity has shifted from 'emotional eater' to 'conscious chooser.' Guilt after eating is rare and quickly resolved. Confidence: 8-9 out of 10.

session_script: [=== SESSION 1: INTAKE, ASSESSMENT, AND EMOTIONAL PAUSE INSTALLATION ===]
[--- WARM-UP AND RAPPORT (5 min) ---]

Jamie, welcome. Thank you for being here today. I know that taking this step takes courage, and I want you to know that this is a completely safe, judgment-free space. There is nothing you can say in this room that I have not heard before, and nothing you are dealing with that is unusual or shameful.

Before we begin, let me tell you what today looks like. We are going to have a conversation first. I am going to ask you some questions about your relationship with food, your eating patterns, and what is going on emotionally when the eating happens. Then I am going to explain how your mind works in a way that will make everything click. After that, we will do hypnosis. And you will leave today with a new tool installed in your subconscious that you can use immediately.
Sound good? Any questions before we start?
[--- L.O.V.E. INTAKE: LISTEN, OBSERVE, VERIFY, EMPATHIZE (15 min) ---]
[L: LISTEN -- open-ended, let them tell their story]
Tell me about your relationship with food. Not what you eat. How you eat. What role does food play in your life beyond keeping your body running?

[[Listen without interrupting. Note: emotional triggers, specific foods, timing patterns, body language when discussing shame/guilt. Watch for: downward gaze when discussing overeating (shame), hand-to-stomach gesture (somatic awareness), pace changes (speeds up when describing the cycle, slows when describing the wish for change).]]
[O: OBSERVE -- reflect what you see and hear]

I notice something important in what you just described. You said you know exactly what to eat, when to eat, how much to eat. The knowledge is all there. But something overrides that knowledge. Something automatic. Something that fires before you can think about it. Is that accurate?
[V: VERIFY -- confirm understanding, get specifics]
Let me make sure I have the full picture. Walk me through a typical day of eating. Start from the morning. What do you eat, when, and where?

[[Map the full daily timeline: breakfast, lunch, dinner, between-meal snacks, after-dinner eating. Identify: (1) which meals are normal versus excessive, (2) where the between-meal eating lives, (3) the critical evening window.]]
Good. Now tell me about the evening. After dinner. What happens between dinner and when you go to bed?
And when the late-night eating happens, what are you feeling right before you reach for the food? Not during. Not after. The moment before. What is the emotion?
[[Expected: stress, loneliness, boredom, dread, emptiness, restlessness. Get the specific emotion. This becomes the target for the Emotional Pause installation.]]
How many nights per week does this happen? Be specific.
And when you eat at night, what are you eating? What are the go-to comfort foods?
[E: EMPATHIZE -- validate, normalize, reframe]

Thank you for being honest about all of that. I want you to hear something clearly. What you just described is not a weakness. It is not a failure of discipline. It is not a character flaw. It is a pattern. An automatic program that your subconscious has been running for years because at some point in your life, it learned that food is the fastest way to change how you feel. And it was right. Food does change how you feel. Immediately. The problem is not that it works. The problem is what happens after.
[--- EATING PATTERN ASSESSMENT (5 min) ---]
Now I want to go deeper on the pattern itself. When you overeat, are you actually hungry? Physically hungry? Stomach empty, body needing fuel? Or is something else driving it?

That is the key distinction. Physical hunger builds gradually, can be satisfied by any food, and stops when the body has enough. Emotional hunger arrives suddenly, demands specific comfort foods, and does not stop when the body is full. Which one are you experiencing most of the time?
Have you tried diets before? Tell me which ones and what happened.

[[Expected: multiple diets, initial success, eventual regain. Listen for the breaking point: what specific event or emotion broke each diet? That breaking point reveals where the subconscious program is strongest.]]
What was the longest you sustained a change in eating? And what broke it? What was the specific moment the old pattern came back?
Here is a question that matters more than any number on a scale. If you could never change your weight, but you could change your relationship with food, what would that look like?
[[This answer reveals the real goal. Write it down verbatim. It becomes the treatment frame for the entire journey.]]
[--- SMART BASELINES (5 min) ---]

Before we go further, I want to establish six baselines. These are all on a 1-to-10 scale. Be honest. There are no right answers. I just need to know where you are today so we can measure the change over the coming sessions.
Number one. Control over eating decisions. 1 means you feel zero control, the eating happens to you. 10 means every bite is a fully conscious choice. Where are you today?

Number two. Awareness of hungry versus eating for other reasons. 1 means you have no idea which is driving you. 10 means you always know whether the drive is physical hunger or emotion. Where are you?
Number three. Ability to stop eating when satisfied. Not stuffed. Satisfied. The point where the body has had enough. 1 means you never stop there. 10 means you always stop at enough. Where are you?
Number four. Emotional eating frequency. How often is your eating driven by emotion rather than hunger? 1 means rarely. 10 means most meals are driven by emotion. Where are you?
Number five. Late-night or stress eating specifically. 1 means it never happens. 10 means it happens every night. Where are you?

Number six. Confidence in your ability to change these patterns. Not willpower. Confidence that the patterns can actually change. 1 means no confidence at all. 10 means absolute certainty. Where are you?
Good. I am recording all six. We will recheck them in two to three sessions and see where the numbers move.
[--- THEORY OF MIND FOR EATING (10 min, conscious education) ---]
Now let me explain what is actually happening in your mind when you overeat. Once you understand this, everything changes.

Your mind operates in two parts. The conscious mind handles about 12 percent of your mental processing. It is the part that knows what to eat, how much to eat, and when to stop. It is where your knowledge lives. It is where your willpower lives.
The subconscious mind handles the other 88 percent. It runs your heartbeat, your breathing, your digestion, your immune system. And it runs your automatic behaviors. Including your eating patterns.

At some point in your life, your subconscious learned a simple equation. Stress equals eat equals feel better. Loneliness equals eat equals comfort. Boredom equals eat equals stimulation. It learned this through thousands of repetitions. And now that equation runs automatically. Before the conscious mind can intervene, the hand is already reaching for the food.

That is why willpower fails. Every time. You are deploying 12 percent of your mental resources against 88 percent. The math does not work. It never will. That is not a character flaw. That is architecture.

Here is the chemistry behind it. Eating triggers dopamine, the reward chemical. Your brain says: that felt good, do it again. Food, especially sugar, fat, and salt, triggers a significant dopamine release. Your gut also produces roughly 90 to 95 percent of the body's serotonin, the calm-and-content chemical. So when you eat, you are literally changing your brain chemistry. The comfort is real. The relief is real. It is neurochemical, not imaginary.

But the effect is temporary. Minutes. Then the dopamine drops. The guilt arrives. The frustration. The self-criticism. And those emotions are themselves triggers for more eating. Trigger, eat, guilt, trigger, eat. The cycle reinforces itself every single time it runs.
We do not fight this cycle with willpower. We update the program. We install a new instruction in the 88 percent so the automatic response changes at the source.
[--- THE EMOTIONAL PAUSE CONCEPT (conscious, pre-trance) ---]
Right now, the pattern runs like this: trigger, then eat. No gap. No pause. No choice. The trigger fires and the hand reaches for food before the conscious mind even registers what happened.
What we install today is a pause between the trigger and the action. The new pattern becomes: trigger, pause, choose, act.

In that pause, which lasts about five seconds, one question rises from your subconscious. Not from willpower. From the deeper mind. The question is: What do I actually need right now? Am I hungry? Or am I feeding something else?
If the answer is hungry, the pause releases. You eat. You enjoy it. No guilt. No shame. Food is fuel and the body deserves fuel.

If the answer is something else, the pause holds. And in that held space, you choose. Breathe. Move. Call someone. Step outside. Drink water. The craving is a wave. It peaks in about 90 seconds and then it passes. Every time. If you can ride 90 seconds, the wave passes. And each time you ride it, the next wave is smaller.

That is what we install today. The Emotional Pause. It goes into the 88 percent. It runs automatically. It does not require willpower. It fires on its own, every time a trigger activates, for the rest of your life.
[--- SUGGESTIBILITY TEST SETUP ---]

Before we begin the hypnosis, I want to do a brief exercise that helps me understand how your mind processes information. This is not a test you pass or fail. It simply shows me whether your subconscious responds more to direct instruction or to indirect imagery. That information helps me tailor everything we do today to the way your mind works best.

[[Run standard suggestibility test: arm rigidity, eye closure, hand clasp, or lemon test depending on client comfort. For Jamie (62% Emotional, Visual), the lemon visualization or book-and-balloon typically work well. Score and note EP confirmation or shift.]]
[--- INDUCTION: ARM-RAISING ---]
[EMOTIONAL LANE (62% Emotional -- primary approach)]
I would like you to sit comfortably with both feet flat on the floor. Place your hands on your thighs, palms down. If you are wearing glasses, please remove them.
Now raise your right arm and bend it at the elbow, placing the palm of your hand in front of your face, about ten inches away, with your fingers pointing upward and above eye level.

Good. Stare at your middle finger. Take a deep, comfortable breath. And on the exhale, you may notice that your fingers begin to separate. Gently. Naturally. Wider and wider, further and further apart.
Now I am going to ask you a few questions. Rather than answering out loud, just nod your head yes or no.

Have you ever been so absorbed in a movie or a book that you forgot where you were? Have you ever driven somewhere and arrived without remembering the drive? Have you ever been so deep in thought that someone had to say your name twice before you heard them?
Good. Can you visualize your hand as it rests in front of you right now? Can you see every detail? The texture of the skin. The lines on your palm. The shape of each finger? Hold that image.
Now I want you to notice something. I will notice the changes happening in your body before you do. When you notice them yourself, simply nod yes.
Your breathing is beginning to deepen. You are taking in more oxygen. When you notice your breathing getting deeper, nod yes.
Your eyelids may begin to flutter. This rapid movement is a natural sign that you are entering the first stages of hypnosis. When you notice this fluttering, nod yes.
Notice that one hand feels heavier against your leg, while the other, the one in front of your face, feels lighter. As if something gentle is lifting it. When you feel this difference, nod yes.

That lightness is growing. Your hand is becoming lighter and lighter. Rising gently. Lifting. Turning slowly inward. Moving closer to your face. Whether your head comes down to meet your hand or your hand rises to meet your face, allow it to happen at whatever pace feels right.
The moment your hand touches your forehead, give me a nod. At that instant you will reach your peak of suggestibility and enter the hypnotic state.
[Wait for contact and nod.] Deep Sleep.

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.
[PHYSICAL LANE BRANCH (use if EP tested Physical)]

[[If suggestibility testing reveals a physical dominant: switch to direct language. 'Stare at your middle finger. Your fingers ARE separating. Your hand IS rising. You WILL feel the difference.' Power words: NOW, IMMEDIATELY, AUTOMATICALLY. Same induction structure, different tone and verb force.]]
[--- DEEPENING: 5-0 COUNT + PHS ---]
Now you can gently allow your hand to float back down to rest comfortably on your lap.
As I count from five down to zero, each number will take you deeper into this comfortable, heavy relaxation.
Five. Going down now. Deeper and deeper. Your body beginning to let go.
Four. Physically releasing. Every muscle softening.
Three. Emotionally calm. Peaceful. Safe.
Two. Mentally quiet. The noise of the day fading.
One. Deeper still. Drifting down.
Zero. [Snap.] Deep Sleep.

Each and every time I suggest the words Deep Sleep to you, for the purpose of hypnosis and with your permission, you will enter this state of hypnosis very quickly, calmly, and deeply, and the physical body will relax.
[--- PROGRESSIVE RELAXATION: BODY RECONNECTION ---]

Now as you rest in this comfortable state, I want you to reconnect with your body. Because your body has been trying to talk to you. It sends signals all day long. Full. Hungry. Tired. Satisfied. And those signals have been drowned out by the noise, the stress, the emotions. Today we turn the volume back up.

Starting at the top of your head. A warm wave of relaxation begins to flow downward. Your scalp softens. Your forehead smooths. The muscles around your eyes release. Your jaw unclenches. And as it does, notice how your body feels when it lets go. That feeling of release. That is your body talking. It is saying: thank you.

The wave moves through your neck. Your shoulders drop. The tension that has been sitting there, maybe for days, maybe for years, it dissolves. Down through your arms. Your hands. Your fingers. Warm. Heavy. Still.

Your chest opens. Your breathing deepens. And now bring your awareness to your stomach. Place your attention there gently. Your stomach is one of the most intelligent organs in your body. It knows exactly when it has had enough. It has been sending that signal your entire life. We are turning up the volume on that signal today.
The warm wave continues. Down through your hips. Your legs. Your feet. Every part of you sinking deeper. Heavier. More connected to the body that has been waiting for you to listen.
Five. Four. Three. Two. One. Zero. [Snap.] Deep Sleep.
[Repeat PHS.]
[--- EMOTIONAL PAUSE INSTALLATION (first taste -- in trance) ---]
Now I want you to imagine a scene. You are at home. It is evening. Around nine o'clock. You have already eaten dinner. The dinner was enough. Your body is satisfied.

And now the feeling arrives. That familiar pull. The restlessness. The urge. Maybe it is stress from the day. Maybe it is the quiet of the apartment. Maybe it is just habit. The old program is firing. It is pointing you toward the kitchen.

But this time, something is different. Between the urge and the action, there is a space. A pause. Like a doorway that was not there before. And in that doorway, a single question forms. Not from willpower. From somewhere deeper. From the part of you that knows the truth.
What do I actually need right now?
Am I hungry? Or am I feeding something else?

And you listen. You listen to your stomach. It is calm. It is satisfied. It does not need food. The hunger is not in your stomach. It is in your chest. It is loneliness. Or stress. Or habit. And now you know.

The pause holds. The doorway stays open. And you choose. You choose to breathe. Three slow breaths. You choose to feel the feeling without feeding it. You choose to let the wave rise and peak and pass. And it does pass. In about 90 seconds. It always passes.

And when it passes, notice what is left. Calm. Clarity. A quiet pride. You did not fight the urge. You did not white-knuckle through it. You simply paused. You asked the question. And you chose. That is the new program. Trigger. Pause. Choose. Act.

This pause is installing itself in your subconscious right now. Deeply. Permanently. From this moment forward, every time an emotional trigger fires, the pause activates automatically. You do not have to remember it. You do not have to force it. It is part of your operating system now. It fires on its own.
And these suggestions grow stronger day by day. Stronger by the hour. Stronger by the minute. They are firmly embedded in your subconscious mind. And they belong to you. They are yours.
[--- COUNT OUT + HOMEWORK ---]
Now I am going to count from zero up to five. With each number you will become more alert, more awake, more refreshed, with a wonderful feeling of confidence and calm.

Zero. I am closing the door to the subconscious mind, sealing in every suggestion. The Emotional Pause is installed. The body connection is restored. The new program is running. Sealing in everything we built today. Sealing out the old automatic cycle.
One. Slowly and calmly beginning to come up.
Two. Becoming more physically aware, more mentally alert. Knowing that tonight, the next time you feel the pull toward the kitchen, the pause will be there. Automatic. Effortless.
Three. Coming up higher now. Feeling wonderful. Feeling lighter. Not because the weight changed. Because the relationship with food just changed.
Four. Your eyes are beginning to open.
Five. Eyes open, wide awake. Fully alert, refreshed, and confident. Welcome back.
One, two, three, four, five. Eyes open, wide awake.
[--- POST-SESSION: HOMEWORK ASSIGNMENT ---]
Before you go, here is what I need from you between now and Session 2. Three things.

First. Keep a food journal. Not calories. Not macros. Write down three things every time you eat: what you ate, what time it was, and what emotion you were feeling. That emotion column is the important one. You will start seeing the pattern on paper.

Second. Practice the Emotional Pause three times a day. Not just when cravings hit. Practice it at mealtimes too. Before each meal, take one breath and ask: am I hungry, or am I feeding something else? If hungry, eat and enjoy. If something else, notice it and choose.

Third. This week, when the late-night urge arrives, try one thing differently. Instead of going to the kitchen, sit with the feeling for 90 seconds. Just 90 seconds. Set a timer if you need to. Notice the wave rise. Notice it peak. And notice it pass. You do not have to do this every night. Just once. One successful ride proves the wave passes.
That is the homework. Food journal with emotions. Pause practice three times a day. One craving ride.
[[Schedule Session 2 within 1-2 weeks. Momentum matters. If the client cannot do next week, two weeks maximum.]]

One more thing. If between now and our next session you have a night where the old pattern runs, where you eat when you did not want to, do not beat yourself up about it. That is the old program firing. It does not erase what we built today. The pause is installed. It may not catch every trigger immediately. But it is there. And it gets stronger every day. What matters is not perfection. What matters is that the pause showed up at least once. That one pause is proof the program is running.
I will see you at Session 2.
[=== POST-SESSION THERAPIST CHECKLIST ===]

[[1. Record all 6 SMART baselines. 2. Note specific triggers identified (which emotions, which times, which foods). 3. Note EP confirmation or shift. 4. Note client's verbatim answer to 'what would your relationship with food look like?' 5. Note any contraindication flags (ED symptoms, depression indicators, medication use). 6. Plan Session 2 focus based on intake findings: if late-night eating is dominant, prioritize Kitchen Closure. If emotional triggers are diffuse, prioritize Satisfied Signal and general mindfulness. If root cause material surfaced strongly, consider moving Root Cause Processing earlier. 7. Send AVS within 24 hours.]]
